title: Kraken Financial First To Secure Fed Account In Rare Move Linking Crypto Banking To US Payment System, Sparking Regulatory Concerns
snippet: Kraken Financial First To Secure Fed Account In Rare Move Linking Crypto Banking To US Payment System, Sparking Regulatory Concerns. Weatherly. 2026/04/12 20:04.
extractedText: MarketsWikiNewsSearchVideosEventsLog in/ Sign upenKraken Financial First To Secure Fed Account In Rare Move Linking Crypto Banking To US Payment System, Sparking Regulatory ConcernsWeatherly2026/04/13 11:04FollowKraken Financial’s direct link to the US Federal Reserve payment network has drawn attention across banking and crypto markets, after its Wyoming-licensed banking arm was granted a tightly restricted account that connects it to core dollar settlement rails for the first time.Kraken Financial Gains Limited Entry To Fed Payment RailsThe Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City approved a limited-purpose account for Kraken Financial on 4 March 2026, marking the first time a crypto-linked firm has been granted direct access of this kind.🚨NEW: @krakenfx, the U.S.’s second-largest crypto exchange, has just done something no other crypto firm has done before: secured coveted access to the Federal Reserve.According to a report by the @WSJ released this morning, the exchange’s banking arm, Kraken Financial, has…— Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett) March 4, 2026The approval applies only to Kraken’s Wyoming-chartered banking unit under a one-year term, not the wider exchange business operated by Kraken.The arrangement allows Kraken Financial to access Fedwire, the US central bank’s wholesale payment system, and hold limited overnight balances.However, the structure is far from a full banking account and remains tightly controlled under an experimental framework.How Restricted Is The Fed Access Structure?The account gives Kraken Financial a direct route into Fed payment infrastructure used by banks to move large-scale funds, reducing reliance on intermediary institutions for certain transactions.It also enables faster settlement in US dollars for wholesale activity.DAYYYYUMN! Go Kraken! This is awesome, but it also means that Kraken will be a fractional reserve. The Fed *only* approves fractional reserves. (It’s a banking industry thing.) https://t.co/ID35pTsqsi— Robert Genito (@RobertGenito) April 12, 2026Still, the scope is narrow.The firm cannot earn interest on reserves, cannot access emergency Federal Reserve lending, and does not have access to ACH or FedNow services under this setup.Reuters also reported that the account does not provide the broader privileges associated with traditional commercial bank master accounts.Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman described the structure as “a bit of an experiment,” reflecting the cautious approach taken by regulators in approving the arrangement.Why The Decision Matters For Crypto Banking AccessThe approval marks a rare point of entry between a crypto-native institution and the US central banking system, an area that has long been difficult for digital asset firms to access directly.Crypto companies have repeatedly pushed for closer integration with traditional payment infrastructure, while regulators and banks have resisted, citing risk and compliance concerns.The decision may influence how future applications from firms such as Ripple, Anchorage Digital, and Wise are assessed.Kraken’s policy head Jonathan Jachym said, “It promotes principles of both safety and soundness, and innovation,” describing the approval as a result of regulatory cooperation.Banks And Lawmakers Raise Risk ConcernsThe decision has triggered criticism from parts of the banking sector and US lawmakers, who question both the process and the risks involved.🏦 KRAKEN FED ACCOUNT: Crypto giant Kraken's landmark Federal Reserve master account faces transparency criticism. Kansas City Fed has Friday deadline to provide info to Democratic lawmakers. Experts warn crypto firms could pose financial stability risks.Source: Reuters #Kraken…— Galaxy Intel (@GalaxyIntel) April 11, 2026The American Bankers Association and 42 state banking associations have objected to the approval, while Representative Maxine Waters has requested further explanation from the Kansas City Fed regarding its legal authority and decision-making process.Concerns raised include money laundering exposure, operational risks, and potential liquidity shifts away from traditional banks.Democrat Lawmakers are demanding answers from the Kansas City Fed over Kraken's master account approval. 👀"Explain how a crypto exchange got approved faster than a chartered bank?” - Rep. Waters to the KC FED 🧐 pic.twitter.com/FswkpoO7SU— Crypto Crib (@Crypto_Crib_) March 27, 2026Richard Levin, chair of the fintech practice at Taft Stettinius & Hollister, shared, “The concern is by introducing institutions that may have less of a track record, less rigorous compliance and operations, even if they have limited models, that it could create a degree of systemic risk.”Fed Governor Michael Barr has also previously highlighted illicit finance risks tied to broader crypto banking exposure.Bitcoin Market Reacts To Institutional SignalMarket participants have linked the approval to growing institutional integration in digital assets, with Bi
